text:
sara: Heads up — seeing a weird eviction/preempt ripple in us-west1 right now. A few GPU nodes report GPUs stuck as allocated even after pods terminated. Impact: batch jobs backfilled onto other nodes and we got a latency spike for small sync inferences.

ken: Oof. Any obvious taint/affinity churn?

sara: Not at first glance. Saw multiple pods stuck in Terminating for ~5-10m. kubelet log shows device-plugin errors re: SDK cleanup.

ops-bot: Deploy alert: rolling restart of gpu-device-plugin on node-gpu-12 at 2026-03-18T13:01Z (auto-restarted by ds).

mike: Can you paste the short kubectl output?

sara: Sure — truncated:
```
NAMESPACE   NAME                              READY   STATUS        NODE          GPUs
ai          trainer-job-3-abcde               0/1     Terminating   node-gpu-12   1/1
infra       gpu-sidecar-ff-123                 1/1     Running       node-gpu-12   0/1
ai          batch-infer-2187                   1/1     Running       node-gpu-09   1/1
```
And node alloc info:
```
kubectl describe node node-gpu-12 | grep -i allocatable -A2
Allocatable:  kubernetes.io/hostname=node-gpu-12
  nvidia.com/gpu: 0
```
So node shows 0 allocatable GPUs despite the node physically having cards.

anya: That sounds like driver/device-plugin mismatch — device-plugin is probably reporting 0 to Kubelet after crash. But why Terminating pods still hold the GPU reservation? Might be the container runtime not releasing?

infra-bot: Prometheus snapshot: gpu_allocated_fraction{node="node-gpu-12"} = 1.0 at 2026-03-18T13:00Z, but kubelet_device_plugin_registered = false since 12:59Z.

ken: If device plugin crashed and kubelet marked plugin as broken, k8s will mark allocatable 0. But pods in Terminating could be stuck waiting for preStop hooks or for the runtime to unmount nvidia devices. Need to force-delete if safe.

sara: I attempted graceful drain, got stuck. Trying `kubectl delete pod <terminating> --grace-period=0 --force` now.

mike: Hold on — before force delete, check if any process is still holding /dev/nvidia* (ssh into node). If driver is hung, force delete will free k8s objects but kernel resources may still be attached to containerd shim and GPU will remain 'in use' at sys level.

sara: ssh'd in: I see containerd-shim for that pod has exited, but nvidia-smi shows MIG instances still present and one process in RIO state pinned to pid 0? weird. I restarted nvidia-docker and device-plugin; nvidia-smi cleared the MIG reservations after daemon restart.

anya: Good. What else caused the ripple? Why did the rest of cluster backfill aggressively?

ken: Our scheduler's binpack policy combined with strict pod-affinity for infer-service forced smaller pods onto remaining GPUs when those nodes were momentarily down. That led to packed nodes and then more preempts when nodes came back. We should add a soft anti-affinity for small infer replicas to avoid full stacking.

mike: Also consider enabling a short cooldown on preemption for Dedicated pool — 30s to 2m might prevent rapid churn when device-plugin flaps.

tanya: Cost/ops question: we had ~8% GPU capacity effectively lost during this. That translates to extra spot usage and some on-demand fallbacks. Can we estimate $$ impact?

ops-bot: Cost estimate (quick): 8% of 120 GPUs in us-west1 = ~9.6 GPUs * 1h = est $3.8/hr (spot delta) based on current rates.

sara: Action items I'm doing: 1) add probe to device-plugin to restart earlier on failure, 2) create a descheduler job to spread high-density small inference pods when fragmentation observed, 3) add a maintenance job to scrub Terminating pods older than 2m in GPU pool (with manual gate).

ken: +1. Also file an infra ticket to audit preStop hooks on training jobs — some are long-running cleanup scripts that block resource release. Maybe migrate long cleanup to background shutdown in training controller.

mike: Quick mitigation: bump kubelet eviction frequency for gpu nodes to reduce prolonged Terminating states. Also patch scheduler to prefer nodes with >0.5 free GPU fraction for new small pods (soft policy).

anya: If we implement soft anti-affinity and descheduler, we should run a canary in a single zone to watch placement churn.

sara: Will open PRs for the device-plugin probe and a descheduler cron. Will also record the incident in incidents/ with timeline + Prometheus links.

tanya: Thanks. Keep us posted — ping @ken @mike when the descheduler cron is live so we can monitor cost impact. :eyes:

ops-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-0318-GPU-LEAKBACK (assigned to sara, severity: medium).

sara: Added logs and short remediation checklist to the ticket. If anyone sees more Terminating pods, drop them here and I'll escalate. :thumbsup:
